answers.answer: NZME engaged external consultants (via the CRD Working Group in May 2023) to support scenario analysis. answers.question: Baseline scenarios
answers.answer: NZME used two baseline climate scenarios: SSP5-8.5 / RCP 8.5 (high emissions, average warming of 4.4 degrees by 2100) and an implied lower-warming scenario. New Zealand reference data was overlaid to these scenarios to develop detailed narratives and parameters to evaluate climate-related risks and opportunities. The scenarios considered time horizons out to the end of this century (2100), drawing on source data including the IPCC 6th Assessment Report, NIWA, Ministry for the Environment National Climate Risk Assessment 2020, NASA, and Shared Socio-economic Pathways.

answers.question: Damage from acute physical risk considered
answers.answer: Yes. NZME considered damage from acute physical risks including: (1) the Ellerslie print plant located in a 1/100 year flood zone (identified as vulnerable to a 1/200 year event in a 2023 risk assessment), (2) transmission equipment vulnerable to disruption from Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle, and (3) the channel/print delivery network vulnerable to disruption from Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle. A full review was conducted in the wake of these weather events, with actions including increasing resiliency in the AM/FM network and improving Business Continuity processes.

answers.answer: The scenarios include sea level rise and flooding (sea and pluvial inundation) as non-temperature variables.
